intro.uz: Bu blogda bir dizayner uydan ishlash tajribasi haqida yozadi. Oʻqishdan oldin oʻylab koʻring: siz uydan ishlashni yoki ofisda ishlashni afzal koʻrasizmi?

paragraphs.en: Two years ago, the small design company where I work decided that most of us could work from home. At first, I was delighted. I would no longer have to spend an hour on a crowded bus every morning, and I could start work in comfortable clothes with a cup of tea next to my laptop. Now, after two years, I want to share what I have learned.

Let me start with the good things. Without the journey, I have gained about two hours every day, and I use some of this time to go for a walk or cook proper meals. I can also concentrate better. In the office, colleagues often stopped by my desk to chat, and it was hard to focus on difficult tasks. At home, I can work for long periods without interruptions.

However, working from home has its problems too. The biggest one for me has been loneliness. Some days I don't speak to anyone except through a screen. I used to have lunch with my colleagues every day, and I miss those conversations more than I expected. It is also harder to ask a quick question, because you have to write a message and wait for an answer.

Another problem is that work and home life can mix together. During my first months, I often answered emails late in the evening and even at weekends. My sister once told me that I was always at work, even when I was sitting at dinner with the family. After a while, I felt tired all the time.

Since then, I have made a few rules for myself. I start and finish work at the same time every day, and I close my laptop when I finish. I have turned a corner of my bedroom into a small office, so I don't work on the sofa any more. Twice a week, I work from a café near my house just to be around other people. My company has also started to organise a team meeting in the office every Friday.

So, would I go back to the office full-time? Probably not. But if someone asked me for advice, I would say that remote work is not for everyone. If you need people around you, a mix of home and office might suit you better.
